title: Tasklets: micro-runbooks + event-driven support automation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Our current runbook corpus is a mix of long procedural docs and ad-hoc scripts. On-call engineers often run multi-step playbooks manually which is slow and error-prone. We need a lightweight, composable abstraction ("Tasklets") to convert discrete runbook steps into idempotent, parameterized tasks that can be executed via CLI, web UI, or triggered from alerts. Goals: 1) reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) for common incidents by 30% via automation and curated step sequences; 2) preserve human-in-the-loop controls for high-risk steps; 3) provide audit trails and RBAC; 4) enable rapid authoring and testing of runbook steps by SREs and support engineers. Scope: implement Tasklet spec, a Tasklet Runner service, CLI integration, Console UI for composing sequences, telemetry hooks (Datadog + tracing), and a sandbox mode for test runs. The work also includes migrating 12 high-frequency runbooks to Tasklet sequences and creating templates for paging vs non-paging incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Tasklet spec documented and reviewed (YAML schema + validation).
Tasklet Runner service deployed to dev cluster with feature flag.
CLI command 'redwood tasklet run' supports dry-run, param injection, and --approve flags.
Console UI allows composing 3-step sequences, saving, and starting workflows with role checks.
All automated runs generate audit entries (who/when/params/outcome) stored in audit-log service.
12 target runbooks migrated and validated end-to-end in staging with telemetry dashboards.
Safety gates: high-risk steps require manual approval; rollbacks supported and tested.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Initial design review: PM liked Tasklet naming but asked to add explicit escalation paths. Action: add 'escalation' field to spec.
2026-02-28 - Engineering sync: decided to implement runner as lightweight Kubernetes job orchestrator rather than long-lived actors to simplify scaling (Jordan).
2026-03-03 - Security requested ability to redact secrets from tasklet params in logs; added requirement to acceptance criteria (audit redaction).
2026-03-08 - UX review: Add a 'preview run' button in Console UI showing simulated steps and estimated side effects (Priya Nair).
2026-03-12 - Implementation update: CLI dry-run working; runner can execute simple shell and API steps. Next: add idempotency tokens and approval hooks.
decisions: Runner architecture: use short-lived Kubernetes jobs managed by Tasklet Controller to leverage existing k8s primitives and avoid a heavyweight orchestration service.
Spec format: YAML-first with JSON schema validation to be compatible with existing authors and the Console editor.
Safety model: default to manual approval for any step that writes to production or changes state; allow policy exceptions via RBAC group 'ops-automation-approver'.
Telemetry: emit structured events to Datadog and tracing spans; surface run-level metrics in Console for SLOs and MTTR tracking.
next_steps: Finish schema definitions: params, idempotency_token, escalation, approval_policy, compensation_steps.
Wire up audit-log integration and ensure redaction before storage.
Complete CLI: implement --approve with OTP fallback and confirmation prompt for destructive flags.
Start migration of 'k8s-restart-db' and 'requeue-ingest' runbooks to Tasklets in staging.
Schedule security review for key management and execution environment on 2026-03-18.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: pre-authorizing safe parameter ranges vs. prompting engineers on each run. We chose pre-authorize + allow override with explicit reason to balance speed and safety. Keep an eye on sprawl of tasklets; add governance (labels + owner) in Console.
